note: Cross-repo contract topology. Pointers only - no schema content, no hashes, no values. Hashes and extracted values live in each consumer's .contracts.lock.json, written by exported/sync_contracts.py. This file changes only when the SET of contracts changes.

contracts.note: A transform, not a byte copy of sources.json: hasCategory/hasAuthor are derived from `strategy` via STRATEGY_FEATURES. Compare against the generated artifact, never against the SSOT.
picker sourceIds are filtered (crawlAvailable OR excludeReason != null), so this differs structurally from categories.json.
List -> {id: label} map. tabconfig.service.ts already fails boot if a sources.json excludeReason has no entry here - that is a partial-copy detector, not a drift detector.

Points at the generated artifact rather than categories.json because the app must mirror what the SERVER emits, and gen_server_categories filters. Today the id/tabMode projection is identical in both. Adding a fixed tab without updating the app mirror is otherwise undetectable - the symptom is zero notifications sent, no error.

Direction matters. The Cloud Function 400s any payload above MAX_TOPICS, so server TOPIC_CAP must stay <= app MAX_TOPICS. `lte` rather than `eq` is what keeps the ADR-0005 deploy order (app first) green at every intermediate step. See skkuverse-server/docs/decisions/0005-notice-dispatch-content-group.md.

Producer does not exist yet (skkuverse-crawler docs/search-mcp-plan.md Phase 1). The ai copy is currently HAND_AUTHORED_TEMPORARY with a _provenance key and a pre-adr-007 schema. Listed while planned so the gap is visible in every `status` run rather than only in a README.

The producer carries the rule set only. Each repo keeps its own .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc naming which paths to lint, and `extends` this vendored block. See conventions/README.md for why the seam falls there.
contracts.blockedBy: Consumers do not vendor the file yet. Land the copy plus its lock entry in each repo first, then flip to active - a lock ahead of activation is safe, the reverse breaks the consumer's default branch.

contracts.note: Three copies exist today; server's and app's are byte-identical except for last-updated, and the umbrella's is an English rewrite. The propagation chain was app -> server -> umbrella by manual copy, which is exactly the pattern the contract system replaces.

contracts.note: The message union a web view may send and the app may receive. web vendors it because the app's package is workspace-private and unpublished. Drift is silent in both directions: parseWebMessage drops an unrecognised type and returns null, so a message the app no longer knows about does nothing at all and raises nothing. Only types.ts is a contract - sender.ts is a three-line platform binding each side owns, and parseWebMessage has no web-side caller.

The palette both design systems render. Before this contract the web view carried these values as hex literals with no import, so a palette change on the app side was invisible until someone compared screenshots. The file is standalone with no imports, which is what makes a byte copy viable.

Shape is React Native idiomatic: lineHeight is absolute px as a number and fontWeight is a string union. web converts to CSS in its own adapter module rather than editing the copy, so this stays a byte copy.
Unitless numbers, so the web adapter appends px. Registered separately from colors because the tool's file contracts carry one producer path each, and a directory has no single hash.

Same shape and adapter as spacing. The producer's sibling token files shadows.ts and duration.ts are deliberately not vendored: their payloads are React Native shadow props and a Reanimated bezier tuple, and vendoring a file no consumer reads adds a gate to maintain for nothing.
